title: Measurement of Telomere Length at the Single Cell Level
protocol: Dissociate the given cells when reaching 90% confluences in a sterile PCR workplace on ice.
Transfer the cell suspension (about 5x10^4 cells) into a 15 ml tube and spin at 1200 rpm for 5 min.
Aspirate and re-suspend the cell pellet with 5 ml of PBS by gently pipetting up and down.
Spin at 1200 rpm for 5 min.
Repeat steps involving aspirating, re-suspending in 5 ml PBS, and spinning at 1200 rpm for 5 minutes.
Aspirate and re-suspend the cell pellet with 1 ml of PBS by pipetting up and down.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 1.5 ml tube and incubate at 4°C for 15 min.
Take out the cell suspension from 4°C.
Pipette out 900 μl of suspension from top carefully with a 1000 μl tip, leaving 100 μl at the bottom.
Mix by pipetting carefully to make the stock of single cell suspension.
Add 4 ml of PBS in an empty ultra-low attachment dish.
Pipette 10 μl stock of single cell suspension into the dish and mix well by pipetting.
Check the density of single cell suspension under a dissecting microscope using a 5X objective lens.
Adjust the density by adding PBS if necessary to ensure no more than 10 cells are visible under microscopic view.
Prepare 1 ml of PBS in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube and set up micropipette with a 75 µm tip.
Look for your target cell under microscope.
Pipette in 1 μl of PBS using the micropipette and place it into the bottom of the dish near your target cell.
Pipette out a little bit of PBS to blow away other cells, then carefully pipette in your target cell.
Transfer 1 μl of PBS containing your single target cell into the bottom of a PCR tube carefully and place the PCR tube on ice.
Wash the micropipette in a clean droplet of media to confirm the cell was moved into the PCR tube.
Repeat steps 11-13 to collect more samples.
Transfer 1 μl of PBS without a single cell into the bottom of a PCR tube to make the first negative control (NTC) tube.
Make several first NTC tubes using the same PBS used for collecting single cell samples.
Add 1 µl lysis buffer into each PCR tube containing samples and 1st NTC.
Spin the PCR tubes briefly.
Place the PCR tubes into the thermo cycler, ensuring they are closed tightly.
Incubate at 75 °C for 10 minutes with a cool down step to room temperature for 5 minutes.
Spin the tubes briefly and transfer them to ice.
Take 4 tubes of single cell lysate and incubate on ice.
Setup pre-PCR master mixes in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube on ice by mixing specified components.
Mix thoroughly by vortexing and spinning briefly.
Aliquot 23 µl of master mix into each PCR tube, including controls and single cell lysate, on ice.
Spin the PCR tubes briefly.
Place all PCR tubes into the thermo cycler and run the specified program.
Purify the pre-PCR product as described in Box1.
Make real-time PCR master mix in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube with Telomere and Alu primers separately according to the following recipe.
Mix well by vortexing and spinning briefly.
Prepare an additional master mix for 48 wells plus extra reactions if necessary.
Set up a 96-well PCR plate with 15 µl of master mix per well.
Add 5 µl of each template DNA sample to corresponding wells.
Ensure templates are added before the master mix to avoid cross-contamination.
Use hESC gDNA at 5 ng/µl for template samples and water for no-template controls.
Spin the PCR plate for 5 minutes at 3000 rpm.
Run the PCR program as specified in Table 7.
Analyze results using default settings in the software.
Set Cq determination mode to “Single Threshold”.
Use “Baseline Subtracted Curved Fit” for baseline setting.
Evaluate SCATR-PCR system performance with control amplifications.
Replace reagents one at a time if contamination occurs during PCR.
Take out 24 tubes of single cell lysate and 1 tube of 1stNTC from the freezer.
Stand the tubes on ice.
Setup PCR reaction master mix in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube by mixing specified components.
Mix thoroughly by vortexing.
Spin the mixture briefly.
Aliquot 23 µl of master mix into each PCR tube on ice.
Spin the PCR tubes shortly.
Place all PCR tubes into the thermo cycler and run the same program as step25.
Purify the pre-PCR product by following Box1 instructions.
Prepare 5 series of standard DNA by 5-fold dilution with water in 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Mix well after making every standard sample.
Let stand on ice after mixing.
Standard samples can be stored at 4 °C for one week.
Setup the real-time PCR master mix in a 2 ml Eppendorf tube with Telomere primers according to the specified recipe.
Mix thoroughly by vortexing.
Spin the mixture briefly.
Make sufficient master mixes for 96 reactions by adding at least 10 extra reactions.
Setup a 96-well PCR plate with 15 µl of master mix plus 5 µl of DNA sample.
Spin the PCR plate for 5 min at 3000 rpm.
Run the same program as step 29 on the spun PCR plate.
Repeat steps 39-41 for Alu primers.
Examine whether there is abnormal amplification plots or not.
Check the Ct value of 2ndNTC for telomere and Alu primers.
Check the real-time PCR efficiency of the standard curves.
Export the data to a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet.
Copy the Cq, Cq Mean, and Cq Std. Dev. of all wells for Tel and Alu to a new Excel file.
Calculate the Coefficient of Variation (CV) for each triplicate using CV = Cq Std. Dev / Cq Mean x 100%.
Check the reproducibility of triplicates by observing the CV.
If the CV is higher than 3%, check the Ct value of the triplicate.
Use the two most similar replicates if one of them is far away from others.
Cut off a sample if its triplicates show high variation.
Check the Ct value of the 1st NTC, which should be around 21-24 and much greater than those of 2ndPTC and samples for both Tel and Alu.
Check the Ct of Alu.
Delete samples with a Ct value close to the 1stNTC as they indicate no template presence.
Calculate the ΔCt for each sample using the formula ΔCt = Ct (Tel) – Ct (Alu).
Determine the ΔΔCt by subtracting ΔCt (2nd PSC) from ΔCt (sample).
Calculate the relative T/R ratio of each sample using the formula Relative T/R ratio = 2-ΔΔCt.
Use GraphPad Prism 6 for statistical analyses.
Compare relative telomere length using unpaired t-test.
Compare variations using F-test.
